main_body: Timber-framed house: a tiled roof with a chimney over a half-timbered upper wall and a stone-brick ground floor with a door
top_band: The roof reads as the top surface, rows 1-43 (brown tile pattern, L=104 and 43, with a light left slope). The eave line at rows 43-45 separates it from the wall face below (L=189).
evidence: The big tiled roof sits above the wall like the Beodeul house roofs. A dark eave row with a brown beam row sits at the roof/wall junction (rows 43-47), and the windows and door have dark inset interiors with sills. The right roof slope is dark and flat and the left slope is thin, so the roof is closer to a front-facing plane than the reference hip roofs. It still reads as a roof slope over a front wall.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours against 185 and 66 in the references. Its median is 3 colours per tile against 18 and 11, and its flat-fill coverage is 17% against 0%. Dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral against 7-9% in the references. Every material (roof, plaster, stone) is one or two tones plus a dark line. The roof tile pattern is a repeated dither with no per-tile highlights, and the plaster and stone are flat beige with dark joints. It looks like a thin, sticker-like 4-colour version next to the rich Beodeul references.
